## TL;DR

Implemented the RepoOS glossary as a VitePress user-docs page, linked it from the docs home page and Settings help area, and added a coverage test that compares glossary entries against the canonical task statuses and review verdicts. The requested Settings and Docs review shots are declared. The required scoped RepoOS check passed, including build/typecheck, all 346 selected test files, rendered contrast, and UI smoke.

## Work and rationale

The task’s code-side vocabulary is defined in `src/core/types.ts` (`STATUSES`) and `src/core/review-verdict.ts` (`REVIEW_VERDICTS`). The verdict list was made a named export so the glossary test can check the actual canonical set instead of maintaining another list that could drift. The test reads the first column of glossary table rows and asserts that every status and verdict is present.

`user-docs/glossary.md` defines the requested shorthand and lifecycle concepts, including MTD, g2g, task states, review verdicts, `needs_input`, hold versus pause, driver, engineer, reviewer, CTO monitor, close-out, landable, handoff, pressureGuard, worktree, easter eggs bundle, preview, shot, gate, round, pass, and narrow resolution. Definitions were checked against the implementation and the repository’s workflow, CLI, close-out, and review documentation. In particular, the page distinguishes `repoos done <id>`—the close-out action—from `repoos mv <id> done`, which only changes task metadata. It also clarifies that hold and pause are controls, not lifecycle statuses.

The page is linked from `user-docs/index.md` and the existing Settings help links. `AGENTS.md` has a one-line pointer. The Settings change uses its established help-link area; shared application styling supplies tooltips for tooltip-enabled UI controls, without adding native browser title tooltips for this feature.

The task’s two requested shots were added with `repoos update 1280 --shots`: the glossary help link at `/settings` in the default app target, and the page heading at `/glossary` in the Docs site target.

## Approaches tried

The status/verdict test was initially placed under `src/core`, but the project’s Vitest discovery tree is `src/ui-app/tests`. It was moved there and imports the canonical source constants. Resolving the Markdown file relative to the test with NodeNext-compatible `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` and `dirname` avoids depending on the runner’s working directory.

The previous handoff attempt reported an index-lock failure while RepoOS was unstaging `repoos.toml` in its main-checkout coordination path. The task explicitly keeps that checkout off limits, so I did not inspect or modify it. Instead, the required changed-path check ran through RepoOS’s remote validation mirror and completed successfully. No staging or commit command was run in this session.

## Challenges and blockers

The remote validation bundle took time to upload, and the changed-path test set was broad. All selected tests completed successfully. The rendered contrast audit examined 17,220 visible text runs over 16 theme scopes and 17 screen states, found no text below the WCAG floor, and passed. The UI smoke test passed at desktop, tablet, and phone widths in light and dark modes. The supplied check command returned success. Handoff finalization remains RepoOS-owned and will report any coordination issue separately.

## Key learnings

The exported status and verdict constants are the right source for glossary freshness checks; comparing against duplicated names would not protect against code changes. `hold` and `pause` sound similar but drive different automation behavior, so the glossary calls out the distinction directly. The repository also distinguishes a successful review verdict from approval and close-out: `good to go` means no blocking review finding, while the separate close-out action merges and records completion.
